import html # Predefined template for user profiles PROFILE_FORMAT = ( "Name: {name}\n" "Biography:\n{about}\n" "Current Status: {status}" ) def display_user_profile(username: str, about: str, current_status: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized and formatted user profile string. Parameters ---------- username : str The user's full name. about : str A multi‑sentence biography provided by the user. current_status : str A brief, current status update from the user. Returns ------- str The sanitized and formatted profile string ready for display on a web page. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not of type `str`. """ # Validate input types if not isinstance(username, str): raise TypeError("username must be a string") if not isinstance(about, str): raise TypeError("about must be a string") if not isinstance(current_status, str): raise TypeError("current_status must be a string") # Sanitize inputs to prevent XSS attacks safe_name = html.escape(username, quote=True) safe_about = html.escape(about, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") safe_status = html.escape(current_status, quote=True) # Format the profile using the predefined template formatted_profile = PROFILE_FORMAT.format( name=safe_name, about=safe_about, status=safe_status ) return formatted_profile
